results.title: Turandot
results.creator_credit: Brian Large, Giuliano Montaldo, National Video Corporation, Radio Televisione Svizzera Italiana (RTSI) and Radiotelevisione Italiana
results.brief_description: Giacomo Puccini’s opera Turandot, with libretto by Giuseppe Adami and Renato Simoni, tells the legend of the beautiful but icy Princess Turandot, and the three riddles she asked her would-be suitors. Performed at the Arena di Verona in 1983 by the Orchestra, Chorus and Corps de Ballet of the Arena di Verona this lavish production with its epic stage setting and beautiful hues of pastel colors features a wonderful cast with Ghena Dimitrova as Turandot, Nicola Martinucci as Prince Calaf, Cecilia Gasia as Liu, Ivo Vinco as Timur. Produced by Giuliano Montaldo, conducted by Maurizio Arena. Sung in Italian. Includes a guide with English translation.

results.title: Weather: rain
results.brief_description:
Episode of Series “For the juniors”.
This video is mostly a visual exploration of rain as it falls on a rain forest. There is a child with yellow rain coat and rain hat walking through the rain and speaking of the rain and how things can be appreciated differently as it falls. The water rushes and runs gathering in streams. The child visits the zoo to watch the animals in the rain who don’t seem as fussed about the rain as humans do, drinking from the sky. The child ends up in the playground enjoying the rain here also.

results.title: Celebrations: new baby
results.creator_credit: Caroline Jones and Australian Broadcasting Corporation
results.brief_description:
Episode of Series “For the juniors”.
A short program aimed at children aged 6-8 outlining the ways people celebrate the addition of a new baby into their lives. Sharing the thoughts of a young boy who meets his new sister for the first time, and then later as they bring the baby home. The way people of different cultures celebrate the birth of a baby are also show, including a Catholic christening and a Vietnamese feast. Each family celebrates the birth in a different way, but all share the same purpose: to welcome a baby into their lives.

results.title: Weather: dry
results.creator_credit: Caroline Jones and Australian Broadcasting Corporation
results.brief_description:
Episode of Series “For the juniors”.
This educational video explains the dry weather and its characteristics. It explains humidity and the effects dry weather has on farms and nature. The video talks of drought and how animals can adapt to periods of dry weather and also the effects of water wastage and conservation. Koalas and camels feature.

results.title: Weather: hot
results.creator_credit: Caroline Jones and Australian Broadcasting Corporation
results.brief_description:
Episode of Series “For the juniors”.
An educational series aimed at 6-8 year olds which covers a variety of subject areas such as weather, transport, space, people and celebrations. When it is hot outside, people wear shorts and t-shirts, drink lots of water, and modify their usual activities to help keep cool. The question is why do we do this? Suitable for children aged 3-7, this video describes how changes in weather affect people, plants and animals differently and the different methods each use to adapt and cope with the heat; what a thermometer is and what it does; how to observe and monitor changes in the weather; and why it is important to dress appropriately when it is hot outside. Also briefly discusses the sun as an energy source.

results.title: Celebrations: achievement
results.brief_description:
Episode of Series “For the juniors”.
A short program aimed at children aged 4-8 narrated by Carolyn Jones showing the different ways that people celebrate achieving certain goals. Following a group of year 7 students to their graduation from school, comparing their preparation and celebration to a group of Police Force cadets preparing to graduate from the Academy. Also discussed is the importance of acknowledging all achievements, no matter how small they may seem.
